This DIY Camper Van Is a Homey Mobile Abode Built for Cross-Country Adventures, It's Now for Sale
26 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Will and Mary Roam
I love a good DIY conversion, not because it's better than a professional one (most aren't), but because they're more attainable to normal people like you and me. Today, I'm checking out a DIY rig that was designed for cross-country adventures.
What we have here is a project based on a 2019 Ram ProMaster 3500 with a 159" wheelbase and a high roof. The two people behind the build are Will and Mary, who are known online as Will and Mary Roam.
As always, let's begin the tour with the exterior. In terms of the wheel and tire combo, the duo kept things simple and opted for standard rims wrapped in road tires.
Most people add ladders to the rear or to the driver's side of the vehicle to be able to climb on the roof. Will and Mary took a different approach and fitted climbing holds on the passenger side, which you can use to climb to the roof, just like you would use in a bouldering gym.
On top of the van, you'll come across three 200 W Renogy solar panels, a Maxxair vent fan, and even a boat hatch skylight. Five wood beams create a small deck that you can chill on – it's the perfect spot to enjoy a coffee while admiring the surrounding views.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Will and Mary Roam The exciting part of the build is the interior, which feels very homey and snug. Regarding aesthetics, the two opted for cream-colored cabinetry, wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring, and a black U-Groove ceiling. The look is complemented by butcher block countertops and a faux tile backsplash.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. However, you can use a large curtain to separate the two areas. What's more, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases.
You can easily turn the front part of the interior into a seating area. Not only can you turn the two cabin seats around to face the back of the van thanks to the swivel bases, but you can also use two tables when seated.
Straight ahead as you enter, you'll come across a unit with a countertop, a silverware drawer, and a 115-liter Dometic fridge with a tiny removable freezer compartment.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Will and Mary Roam Beside it, the couple added a decently sized bench that hides a Nature's Head composting toilet on a slide-out, with its backrest integrating two storage compartments. Moreover, above, you'll find two cabinets.
Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side. It features a propane-powered RecPro oven with a three-burner stove and a deep stainless steel sink with a rotating faucet. What's more, a Maxxair vent fan above draws out the smells and fumes from cooking.
An overhead cabinet, a drawer, a toiletry storage compartment, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage. The latter houses a sealed compartment with a propane canister.
The largest storage spot in this van is a floor-to-ceiling unit opposite the kitchen. It offers a closet with hanging space and two large shelves. What's more, the unit's tall door has a full-length mirror on the inside.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Will and Mary Roam Like in the majority of camper vans, the rear part of the living space is taken up by the bedroom. It boasts a full-size memory foam mattress, two overhead cabinets, charging points, two bunk windows with sliding screens, and a skylight above that's big enough to climb through.
Finally, the space underneath the bed was turned into a garage that's accessible only from the back of the van, after opening the rear doors.
The garage is split into three key parts: two boxes on the sides that accommodate the utility systems, and a big open space in the middle filled with tools and a bunch of other stuff.
Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are a 300 Ah Renogy battery bank and a 2,000 W Xantrex inverter. Three charging sources allow you to keep the batteries topped off: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC alternator charging while the engine is running.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Will and Mary Roam On plumbing, the van is equipped with a 39-gallon (147-liter) freshwater tank, a 36-gallon (136-liter) greywater tank, a water pump, an accumulator, a three-stage Clearsource water filtration system, and an outdoor shower connection.
You'll also notice Van Essential storage pockets attached to the inner part of the two doors, which create a lot of useful storage space out of a spot that would've been otherwise useless. Moreover, the passenger-side door holds two towel hooks.
All in all, Will and Mary did a fantastic job with this conversion, packing all the basic comforts most people would need to travel across the United States full-time.
The duo has already put the van to the test by completing a full lap around the country this year, and now they've put it up for sale. According to its Vancamper listing , it has 97,500 miles (156,911 km). Will and Mary are offering it for $59,999 (€54,254), after dropping the price from $65,000.
